items.stem: According to Kepler's third law, a satellite in a higher orbit has what orbital period compared with a lower one?

options.rationale: Correct: period increases with orbital size under Kepler's third law.
Higher orbits have longer, not shorter, periods.
Period depends on orbital size, so it differs.
A finite orbit always has a finite, non-zero period.

items.explanation: Correct: period increases with orbital size under Kepler's third law.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about orbital manoeuvres are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A Hohmann transfer is an energy-efficient two-burn transfer between circular orbits
options.rationale: Correct: the Hohmann transfer is the classic efficient two-impulse transfer.

options.text: Plane changes generally require significant delta-v
options.rationale: Correct: changing orbital plane is delta-v expensive.

options.text: Manoeuvres require no propellant at all
options.rationale: Manoeuvres require delta-v, which costs propellant.

options.text: Orbits can be changed instantly with no energy
options.rationale: Changing an orbit always requires energy/delta-v.

items.explanation: Correct: the Hohmann transfer is the classic efficient two-impulse transfer.

items.stem: Why does a satellite in low Earth orbit gradually lose altitude over time?

options.text: Residual atmospheric drag removes orbital energy
options.rationale: Correct: thin upper-atmosphere drag slowly decays low orbits.
Gravity does not switch off; it acts continuously.

options.text: The satellite speeds up and escapes
options.rationale: Drag slows and lowers the orbit; it does not cause escape.
Radiation pressure is small and not a simple downward push.

items.explanation: Correct: thin upper-atmosphere drag slowly decays low orbits.
